# Recreation Prompt

Recreate `Rizz Runner: Neon Pipe Rally`, a portrait-first browser endless runner. The protected game is a one-thumb platform runner: tap/click/Space/ArrowUp to jump, tap again midair for one double-hop, land on scrolling platforms, avoid red hazard tiles, score when safe platforms pass behind the player, speed increases with score, and failure happens on hazards or falling.

The authored world is a satirical Mario-inspired cyber Y2K meme arcade. The focal actor is Cap Kid, a neon cap-wearing shonen runner chasing clout in a friends lobby. Safe platforms are holographic pipe rails with coin studs. Hazards are red `NO RIZZ` glitch pits. The HUD uses `CLOUT`, restart copy says `Run It Back`, and failure says `Rizz Patched`. Visuals should be procedural canvas/CSS: neon city parallax, scanline grid, meme stickers, chunky arcade panels, and mobile-readable CTAs.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a mobile canvas endless runner. A fixed-x player jumps with tap/click/Space/ArrowUp, can double-jump, lands on scrolling platforms, gains score when normal platforms pass behind the player, accelerates as score rises, and loses by falling or touching red kill platforms.

## Protected mechanics
- One-thumb tap/click jump and keyboard jump.
- Double-jump limit of two jumps before landing.
- Gravity/vertical velocity movement with fixed horizontal player position.
- Left-scrolling platforms with score-based speed escalation.
- Platform landing collision, kill-tile collision, fall failure.
- Score increments only when normal platforms are passed.
- Start, fail, and instant restart loop.

## Remixed target
`Rizz Runner: Neon Pipe Rally` reframes the same loop as a cyber Y2K satirical plumber-parody arcade run. The player is Cap Kid, a neon shonen runner farming clout across holographic pipe rails while dodging de-rizz glitch pits in a friends-lobby score attack.

## Safe theming surfaces
HUD vocabulary, start/fail copy, player drawing, platform/hazard drawing, background, particles, fonts, feedback GIFs, audio wiring, panel styling, and progression labels are safe to transform without changing mechanics.
